source.title: Risk and Rizq
source.summary: How Islamic concepts of divine provision and chance gave the world the vocabulary of uncertainty, insurance, and entrepreneurship.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: The word "hazard" comes from al-zahr, Arabic for dice. Explore how the Islamic concept of rizq (divine provision) created a culture of entrepreneurial risk-taking, how the prohibition of gharar (excessive uncertainty) shaped contract ethics, and how Khadijah bint Khuwaylid embodied the merchant spirit. From mudaraba partnerships to modern takaful insurance, now a $50 billion industry.

thread: The word "hazard" comes from al-zahr, Arabic for dice.
Islamic merchants created the vocabulary of uncertainty that still shapes how we talk about risk. They needed precise language for what could and couldn't be bought and sold.
The concept of gharar — excessive uncertainty that corrupts contracts — gave birth to entire industries built on managing what we cannot know.
Modern takaful insurance is now a $50 billion industry, all rooted in ancient debates about divine provision and human responsibility. Listen: https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-tt-5

linkedin.post: The word "hazard" comes from al-zahr, Arabic for dice — a reminder that Islamic civilization gave us not just goods and gold, but the very language of uncertainty. Medieval Muslim merchants faced a fundamental question: how do you build trust across vast distances when you're trading in things you cannot fully predict or control? Their answer shaped concepts we still use today: risk, hazard, and the ethics of uncertainty in contracts. The Islamic principle of gharar — excessive uncertainty that corrupts agreements — wasn't just legal theory. It was practical wisdom that helped merchants distinguish between acceptable business risk and speculative gambling. From mudaraba partnerships to modern takaful insurance (now a $50 billion industry), these frameworks continue to offer insights for contemporary finance. Listen: https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-tt-5
